facts.text: Willisville began as a small rural settlement in the late 19th century, originally an agricultural outpost in southwestern Perry County.
The village’s name comes from Dickie Willis, an early figure who helped develop the area.
Early settlers favored wooded sections over open prairies, building family farms that grew corn, wheat, potatoes, and livestock.
By the early 1900s, Willisville had become a community hub, thanks to its strategic location near emerging railroad lines.
The local economy today employs around 193 people, mostly in health care and social assistance, reflecting its role as a bedroom community near Pinckneyville.
Willisville sits near the Kaskaskia River, exemplifying Midwestern small‑town life with an economy centered on agriculture, health care, and limited manufacturing.
